acceptance_criteria: For every durable administrative identity operation, the route must use the operation-specific atomic mutation plus completion-audit/outbox method when atomic support is advertised; partial capability must fail closed before mutation. Any generic non-atomic fallback must be explicitly limited to a volatile development identity and disabled for production and production-safe composition.

Tenant-scoped authority must not mutate global email/password/profile state or the shared role_version for an account with memberships in another tenant. Check role, grants and permission overrides as well as credentials. A rejected request must leave the user, memberships, sessions, versions and outbox unchanged.

PostgreSQL create/update/deactivate/reset must commit the intended identity changes and completion event atomically, roll back when outbox writing fails, keep deactivation tenant-scoped, and preserve safe direct/legacy entry points.

The outbox projection must be idempotent, bounded and recoverable, with bounded retries/dead-letter/manual retry, concurrency safety, worker runtime composition and restart recovery supported by implementation and tests.
Evidence must substantiate the claims using API regressions and actual disposable PostgreSQL behavior. Identify any concrete failure path, missing test, false claim or residual risk.
